title: Notifications docs
intro: Notifications sends WhatsApp, e-mail, SMS, browser push, staff push and webhooks for your website, through your own provider keys. Other products send through it with the Notifications server token pasted into their Connections; your own server sends with the same API. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so what you send there is sent for real. There is no test mode.
send: Send a message with the server token: POST /v1/messages/<channel> (email, sms, whatsapp, push or staff-push) with the template key, the recipient and the values. The answer (201) is the message as the delivery log keeps it: status sent, queued (waiting for its time), retrying, failed or skipped (unsubscribed or over a send limit). Send an Idempotency-Key header so a repeated request is refused instead of sent twice.
templates: Templates live in Notifications: one per template key, channel and language, written in the product dashboard (Settings → Templates) or in the template editor widget. Write {name} where a value goes. Template keys of other products' own events start with the product id (accounts., ecommerce., chat., payments., growth.) and work while the channel is on; every other key is yours and needs the Merchant send API feature. A required message (sign-in codes, order and account updates) is always sent; any other message is optional and is not sent to people who unsubscribed. Optional messages can use {unsubscribeUrl}; e-mails also get one-click unsubscribe headers. An urgent message ignores quiet hours.
retries: A message that fails is tried again on the same channel up to 3 times, on the next uses of your website after 1 and 5 minutes (there are no background jobs, so on a quiet site it waits for the next request). Then, with the Fallback channel feature, it is sent once on the fallback channel set in Settings (for example WhatsApp, then SMS) when the recipient has that address and a template exists for it. Every attempt is in the delivery log, kept forever in your own database.
timing: Quiet hours hold messages that are not urgent until the end of the quiet window in the recipient's time zone (to.timeZone, else the time zone in business.json). Send limits skip messages over the hourly or daily cap per recipient. Delayed send takes sendAt (ISO-8601); the message goes out on the first use of your website after that time, so it can be late on a quiet site.
languages: With Multi-language templates on, a template can have a version per language. The recipient's language (language, else to.language) picks the version: the exact code, then its base language (pt for pt-BR), else the default version.
providers: Connect a provider per channel in the product dashboard (Connections). E-mail: SMTP, Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun or Amazon SES. SMS: Twilio, or any gateway over HTTP. WhatsApp: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API, Twilio, or any gateway over HTTP (for example Connectivity.pk). A gateway over HTTP takes the address, json or form, optional headers as a JSON object and a body template where {to}, {toDigits}, {text} and {secret} are filled. Example for Connectivity.pk: address https://connectivity.pk/api/messages/chat, form, body instance_id=<your instance>&token={secret}&to={toDigits}&body={text}&priority=0.
keywords: Unsubscribe keywords: point your provider's incoming-message webhook at the address below. Twilio requests are checked with your auth token; the WhatsApp Cloud API with the app secret (and the verify token for its first check). A reply that is one of the keywords in Settings unsubscribes that number from optional messages.
push: Browser push: create a P-256 key pair (VAPID, for example with npx web-push generate-vapid-keys) and enter it in Connections → Push keys. Copy the service worker below to the root of your website as /ss-notifications-sw.js, then place the push-permission widget. When a visitor turns notifications on, the widget fires the ss-notifications:subscribed event on window with { subscriberId } and keeps it in localStorage; send it to your server and link it to your user, then send with to: { subscriberId }. Staff push works the same way in your admin with a ticket (permission push.subscribe); send with to: { staffId } (the user id in the ticket).
webhooks: Outgoing webhooks: add up to 5 https URLs in Settings and a random signing secret (at least 24 characters) in Connections. Each event is a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Check it before trusting the body, and refuse times older than 5 minutes. A failed delivery is retried up to 5 times on later uses.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widget where it should appear. Widgets render nothing while their feature is off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: the delivery log (log.read), the template editor (templates.edit), send a message (messages.send) and staff notifications (push.subscribe). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
